function: Over-the-air aggregation of model updates of pruned and quantized DNNs from many devices by analog superposition over a Rayleigh fading channel with AWGN (pp. 4, 6-7).
system: One parameter server, E=50 or 100 edge devices at 50 m; OFDM subchannels, 20 MHz bandwidth, 2.4 GHz center frequency; antenna configuration not stated; no RIS (p. 7).
method: Magnitude pruning (30/50/70%) and quantization-aware training (FP16, INT8) with fine-tuning on ResNet50 and InceptionV3, trained by federated averaging with SGD, supervised classification (pp. 4-7).
data_channel: MNIST and CIFAR-10, i.i.d. partition; simulated Rayleigh fading with i.i.d. gains, AWGN, path loss at 2.4 GHz; average SNR up to 10 dB (pp. 7, 9).
test_conditions: Each setting trains an FL model (up to 1000 epochs), tested on the dataset test split: E=50 or 100, SNR 5 or 10 dB, SNR sweep (pp. 7-11).
baselines: Uncompressed model as ideal reference, plus the paper's own pruned, quantized and combined variants; no earlier compression or aggregation design compared (pp. 7-8, 12).
metrics: Test accuracy, model size (MB), convergence epochs, OTA acceleration factor (size ratio times convergence ratio), theoretical operation energy and power (pp. 8-14).
complexity: Model sizes in MB (Table III), parameters and OFDM frames of uncompressed models (Table II), multiplication and addition counts with energy (Table V); no aggregation cost (pp. 7-8, 14).
q1_support: p. 7: "has Rayleigh fading effect with i.i.d. gains on the transmitted GVs"; own Rayleigh plus AWGN simulation with a free-space path-loss term (Table II), no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 7: "We then observe the effects of varying SNR on the accuracy of uncompressed ResNet50 and corresponding compressed versions of ResNet50"; a sweep with convergence curves per setting (Figs. 10-13), and no trained model is tested on unseen conditions.
q3_support: p. 7: "the accuracy of the model is termed as UC accuracy/ideal accuracy"; the only reference is the uncompressed model and the paper's own variants, with no earlier published compression or aggregation design compared.
q4_support: p. 13: "calculate the energy requirements for addition and multiplication operations for various models"; sizes, operation counts and energy (Tables II, III, V) are costs of the models being trained, not of an aggregation or transceiver design.
q5_support: p. 7: "We utilize MNIST and CIFAR-10 data sets to train ResNet50 and InceptionV3 DNNs"; learning-task datasets do not count, the channel is simulated, and no code or data link is given.
notes: Title and DOI on p. 1 match. Borderline inclusion: the contribution is compression of the models aggregated over the air (analog superposition over Rayleigh plus AWGN, no designed transceiver or power control), so area 7 holds only if OTA-FL efficiency counts as the aggregation problem; otherwise exclude as function. q4 is borderline: Table V (p. 14) lists multiplication and addition counts and energy of the compressed models, treated as the cost of the trained model under the OTA-FL rule.
